closureReason: The original AI masonry used stacked/grid joints; precise-object-edit did not correct it reliably; deterministic texture projection produced an offset bond but remained flat, skewed and visually artificial; a human decision changed House A to a light rendered/plastered facade.
geometryRole: visual material rule only; never canonical building geometry

immutableVisualRules: Horizontal courses use one consistent brick and joint scale.
Every adjacent course offsets head joints by half one horizontal module.
No vertical head joint may continue through adjacent courses.
Pattern geometry remains deterministic; photographic color and low-frequency illumination come from A01.

physicalDimensionSource.title: Målafsætning – Mur & Tag
verifiedFacts: Danish normal-format brick declared dimensions are 228 × 108 × 54 mm.
Three masonry courses equal 200 mm, yielding a 66.6667 mm vertical course module.

materialReference.role: light warm brick color, mortar character, texture, illumination and photographic variation only
materialReference.supersededAspect: A01 stacked/grid head-joint geometry is rejected and is never sampled as pattern geometry

reasons: The corrected patch remains visibly smoother and flatter than the surrounding A01 masonry.
The transition between the deterministic patch and the photographic source remains perceptible.

maskRules: Only pixels inside the four-point facade-plane mask may change.
The selected test patch contains no opening, roof, gutter, downpipe or foreground vegetation.
A deterministic twelve-pixel smooth feather is permitted at the mask boundary.
testPatch.projection: inverse projective homography from destination image quad to the deterministic masonry plane
testPatch.photographicPreservation: low-frequency A01 color and illumination plus bounded source detail; low-contrast mortar; deterministic micro-variation; original pixels outside mask
